text:
Alex: Heads up — I noticed a delta on ACME Corp's private VPC invoice. Our cloud bill shows NAT egress and per-GPU license line items for their reserved cluster, but the customer-facing invoice only has the monthly reserved capacity charge. Are we supposed to pass NAT/egress through or include it in the reserved price?

Maria (Finance): @Alex good find. We had discussed re: pass-through for cloud egress historically, but I thought on private deployments we bundled networking into the recurring fee. Need to check contract terms for ACME.

Sahil: From infra side — the NAT is shared across multiple tenants in that region's private-hosted setup. Metering per-customer was never enabled on that NAT. If we unbundle, we'll need per-customer SNAT IPs and cost tagging, which isn't in the current runbook.

Ops SRE: Agree with @Sahil. We also saw a spike last month due to backup transfers — that caused a larger NAT bill. Did ACME have any exports?

Alex: We checked logs — ACME's cluster did a large transfer to an external analytics partner on 2026-02-11. That's when egress spiked. I've pasted the invoice fragment below:

```
Line item: NAT Gateway - us-west-2 - $12,430.24
Line item: GPU License (reserved) - 4xA100 - $6,400.00
Line item: Reserved Capacity monthly - ACME - $10,000.00
```

Maria (Finance): Ugh. Contracts team wording: "Customer pays network egress and third-party cloud usage incurred by Customer's private deployment." But billing ops passed only reserved capacity as the invoiceable item for this engagement historically.

Karen (Customer Ops): ACME will push back if we suddenly add a NAT line mid-quarter. They asked for predictable billing. Any options?

Sahil: Short term: we can absorb this one spike and flag it as extraordinary. Long term: we need per-customer meter tags for NAT and GPU license mapping. That requires a change to provisioning: assign customer-specific EIPs and per-tenant subnets.

BillingBot: Automated note: Found unmatched cloud charges for account nh-12345 between 2026-02-01 and 2026-02-28 totaling $14,820. Suggestions: create cost allocation tags, enable flow logs for meter reconciliation.

Maria (Finance): Proposal: absorb February's NAT spike, open a billing change request for future contracts, and issue a CTO-engage note for infra to estimate effort & cost to enable per-customer NAT metering.

Alex: Sounds reasonable. Can infra estimate effort/ETA? Also need to know if GPU license per-GPU is allowed to be passed separately under existing SOW.

Sahil: I'll scope this week: estimate includes changes to provisioning templates, tagging, and ops playbooks. Probably 3 sprints to get reliable meterable NAT per customer, plus testing.

Ops SRE: Also need to update our invoice generator to accept extra line items (NAT egress, per-GPU license). That's a small billing-engine change.

Maria (Finance): I'll check SOW and talk to Legal re: retro changes. If Legal ok, we'll draft a one-off amendment for ACME. For now finance will absorb Feb and flag for cost center write-off.

Karen (Customer Ops): I'll prep a customer communication template in case of pushback. Keep me posted when there's an ETA.

Alex: Great. Action items: @Sahil scope infra changes (due EOD Fri), @Maria validate SOW/legal, @Ops SRE estimate billing-engine work. I'll add a note to the ACME ticket. :thumbsup:

Sahil: On it.

Maria (Finance): Will follow up.

BillingBot: Ticket created: BIL-4821 - ACME NAT reconciliation.
